q: 51. The value of the property (without being dismantled) at the end of the useful life period is known as
explain: Salvage value is the estimated value of an asset at the end of its useful life without being dismantled. If the asset is dismantled and sold as material, it is called scrap value.

q: 52. The annual periodic payments made for the repayment of the capital invested is known as
explain: Annuity is a fixed sum of money paid to a person at fixed intervals (usually annually) for a certain number of years or for life.

q: 53. The gradual accumulation of amount by way of annual periodic deposits which is meant for the replacement of the structure at the end of its useful life period is known as
explain: A sinking fund is created by setting aside a small amount of money every year so that at the end of the building's life, the accumulated amount is enough to rebuild or replace the structure.

q: 54. The thickness of slabs and beam must be measured to the nearest
explain: While most dimensions are measured to 0.01m, the thickness of slender concrete members like slabs and beams is often specified to be measured to the nearest 0.005m (5mm) for higher precision.

q: 55. Wood work for doors and windows is measured in
explain: Woodwork for frames (chowkhats) is measured in cubic metres (m³), whereas the door/window shutters are measured in square metres (m²).

q: 56. Unit of measurement of supply of brick is
explain: Bricks are manufactured as individual units and are supplied, counted, and paid for by number (usually per 1000 units).

q: 57. The unit of measurement of marble skirting is
explain: Skirting is a linear feature along the base of walls. Since its width/height is fixed, it is measured in running metres (per m).

q: 58. The unit of measurement of terrazzo or marble or tile flooring is
explain: Flooring is a surface treatment and is measured by the total area covered in square metres (m²).

q: 59. The unit of measurement of pile driving is
explain: Pile driving is generally measured by the depth of penetration into the ground, expressed in running metres (per m).

q: 60. The unit of measurement of lintel over opening is
explain: Lintels are structural concrete members and are measured by their total volume in cubic metres (m³).

q: 61. The unit of measurement of iron hole fast is
explain: Hole fasts are small iron fittings used to secure frames to walls; they are estimated and paid for by their weight (kg).

q: 62. The life of brick work work is generally assumed to
explain: First-class brickwork in cement mortar is considered highly durable and is usually assigned a useful life of 100 years in valuation.

q: 63. The depth of shallow manhole is taken as
explain: Manholes are classified by depth; those up to 2.1 metres are generally considered shallow or medium manholes.

q: 64. The number of corrugations in a G.C.I. sheet is
explain: A standard Galvanized Corrugated Iron (GCI) sheet typically contains 10 corrugations (5.5 inches pitch) for a standard width sheet.

q: 65. The expected out turn of brick work in cement mortar in foundation and plinth per mason per day, is
explain: For brickwork in the foundation and plinth (which is simpler than superstructure), a mason is expected to complete 1.25 m³ per day.

q: 66. The unit of measurement of supply of pipe (diameter and type specified) is
explain: Pipes for plumbing or sewage are specified by their internal diameter and are measured by their length in running metres (per m).

q: 67. The unit of measurement of sawing timber  is
explain: Sawing timber is usually measured in m^2

q: 68. The unit of measurement of plantation of tree (diameter and type specified) is
explain: Planting rows of trees or hedges is often measured linearly in running metres (per m) or sometimes per number for individual trees.

q: 69. The volume of cement in one bag is
explain: One bag of cement weighs 50 kg. Given the density of cement (~1440 kg/m³), the volume is 50/1440 ≈ 0.0347 m³, commonly taken as 0.035 m³.

q: 70. The concealed faces of the frames of doors and windows are painted with
options: two coats of enamel paint which is applied for the rest of the frame
explain: The faces of the wood frame that come into contact with the masonry are painted with coal tar to protect the wood from moisture and termite attack.

q: 71. The information which cannot be included in drawing is conveyed to the estimator through
explain: Specifications describe the quality of materials, workmanship, and methods of construction which cannot be fully explained in a technical drawing.

q: 72. The area of the segmental portion of an arch with span l and riser r is approximately given by
explain: The area of a parabolic or shallow segmental arch is roughly calculated as two-thirds of the product of the span and the rise (2/3 × l × r).

q: 73. In which of the following works, the work turned in cu. m per mason per day will be the least
options: random rubble masonry in lime mortar
explain: Stone arch work is highly skilled and time-consuming because of the precise shaping and fitting of stones (voussoirs), leading to the lowest daily out-turn.

q: 74. The volume of cement required to prepare 100 cu. m of 1 : 2 : 4 concrete is
explain: Dry volume required is 1.54 × 100 = 154 m³. Volume of cement = 154 / (1+2+4) = 154 / 7 = 22 m³. Option 'd' (21 m³) is the closest standard approximation.

q: 75. Which of following is known as general overhead?
explain: General overheads include office expenses, rent, stationery, and travelling expenses of the contractor's staff that aren't specific to one single task.

q: 76. Which one is overhead expenditure of the following items
explain: Establishment charges refer to the cost of maintaining the organization and permanent staff, which is a significant component of overheads.

q: 77. A revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate exceeds
explain: A revised estimate is a fresh estimate of the revised quantities and rates. It is generally required when the original sanctioned estimate is likely to be exceeded by more than 5%.

q: 78. In a detailed estimate the provision for contingencies is usually
explain: Contingencies represent incidental expenses of a miscellaneous character which cannot be reasonably predicted; 3% to 5% of the total cost is the standard allowance.

q: 79. The expected out turn of 2.5 cm cement concrete floor per mason per day
explain: For thin concrete flooring (2.5 cm thick), a mason is expected to finish an area of approximately 7.5 square metres in a standard working day.

q: 80. The expected out turn for earth work in excavation in ordinary soil per mazdoor per day is
explain: For manual excavation in ordinary soil up to a depth of 1.5m, the standard task work for one laborer is 3.00 cubic metres.

q: 81. Size, capacity and materials need be specified for
explain: Plumbing fixtures and valves must be defined by their dimensions, flow capacity, and material (e.g., brass, CP, PVC) for accurate pricing in an estimate.

q: 82. In case of laying gullies, siphons, intercepting traps, the cost includes
explain: The unit rate for specialized sanitary traps includes the physical placement, the concrete base (bedding), and the labor for jointing them to the pipe network.

q: 83. Cost of fittings and their fixing is specified for the following sanitary fittings
explain: Major sanitary items are typically estimated as 'sets' which include the primary fixture plus all necessary brackets, pipes, and fixing labor.

q: 84. The detention period in septic tank is assumed
explain: In the context of small-scale septic tanks, the theoretical minimum detention time for liquid to settle is often considered around 30 minutes, though design storage usually spans 24-48 hours.

q: 85. The minimum width of a septic tank is taken
explain: Standard design codes recommend a minimum width of 750 mm (75 cm) for a septic tank to allow for proper cleaning and maintenance.

q: 86. The trap which is provided to disconnect the house drain from the street sewer is called
explain: An intercepting trap is placed at the last manhole of the house drainage system to prevent foul gases from the public sewer from entering the house pipes.

q: 87. The inspection pit or chamber is a manhole provided in a base drainage system
explain: To prevent blockages and facilitate cleaning, inspection chambers are required at any change in the line or level of the pipe and at regular intervals on straight runs.

q: 88. Normally the ratio of span to effective depth of a beam is
explain: For simply supported beams, a common rule of thumb for preliminary sizing is a span-to-depth ratio between 10 and 12.

q: 89. The unit weight of R.C.C. in kg/m³ is
explain: Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC) is generally assumed to have a unit weight of 2400-2500 kg/m³ (24-25 kN/m³).

q: 90. One metric horse power is equal to
explain: In the metric system, 1 HP (Metric) = 735.5 Watts or approximately 0.736 kW.

q: 91. The unit of measurement of mass, voluminous and thick work like E/W, B/W etc is
explain: Earthwork (E/W) and Brickwork (B/W) exceeding 15cm thickness are measured by their total volume in cubic metres (m³).

q: 92. If the payment of annuity begins after some years in future, it is known as
explain: A deferred annuity is a type of annuity contract that delays payments until the investor chooses to receive them in the future.

q: 93. To account for the corrugations, the plain area of the semi-corrugated asbestos sheet is increased (for white washing)
explain: For corrugated surfaces, the flat area is increased by a percentage (10% for semi-corrugated, 20% for corrugated) to account for the actual surface area being painted/washed.

q: 94. Specifications for the hold fasts are given in terms of
explain: In detailed specifications, steel hold fasts for door frames are estimated by their weight (usually in kg).

q: 95. If valuable properties are found during excavation, it becomes the property of
explain: Under most national 'Treasure Trove' laws, any antiquities or valuables discovered during excavation belong to the State/Government.

q: 96. The volume of sand a normal truck can carry per trip is approximately
explain: A standard truck (tipper) used for residential construction usually carries about 100 to 150 cubic feet, which translates to roughly 3-5 cubic metres.

q: 97. The item of the brick structure measured in sq. m, is
explain: Brick edging (as for pathways) or thin brick soling is measured in area (sq. m) or length (m), unlike structural brickwork which is cubic.

q: 98. Pick up the item whose weight is added to the weight or respective item, is
explain: When estimating structural steelwork by weight, the weight of small connecting components like cleats, brackets, and bolts is added to the main member's weight.

q: 99. The reduced levels of points, 30 metres apart along the longitudinal section of a road portion... is
explain: In surveying, chainage is recorded as 'Chain + Links'. For 30m intervals, 15 chains (if using 20m chain) or specific local link counts are used to designate the station.

q: 100. The cross-section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is shown in figure. The area of the shaded portion is
explain: This formula represents the cross-sectional area of a road in 'side-hill' work where one portion is in cut and another in fill, depending on the side slope (s) and transverse slope (r).
